summary: The ACCV 2026 draft (/home/spencer/Projects/OnlineSyntheticCorrespondence/ACCV_2026/main.tex, 1059 lines, compiles to 23 pp + 9 pp supplement) argues a single thesis: which synthetic training set transfers best to a real correspondence benchmark is regime-conditional, because the training regime determines which of two directed motion-mismatch costs the model pays. In BFV motion space (4-D normalized flow vectors), d_T->B measures off-target mass (precision-analogous) and d_B->T measures missing support (recall-analogous). The "regime-direction principle": from-scratch models pay BOTH costs (so candidate utility tracks the sum d_TB+d_BT, which equals the symmetric average), while a pretrained image-feature backbone forgives off-target mass, leaving missing support as the sole cost; because the two distances are anti-correlated across natural sources (mean Spearman ~-0.35, tight-vs-broad tradeoff), averaging the forgiven cost back in actively corrupts pretrained rankings. Argument structure: Sec 1 states the principle and 5 contributions; Sec 2 positions vs Mayer et al. (undirected), transferability estimation (symmetric/classification-only), and precision-recall divergences (diagnostic, not predictive); Sec 3 defines the 99-model / 891-measurement transfer study (CATs++, RAFT, GLU-Net in 9 variants x 11 sources x 9 benchmarks, peak PCK@0.05, Middlebury excluded), the two NN distances, support-vs-density estimator argument, and the anchor+ranking decomposition; Sec 4 establishes the flip (8 of 9 variants, exact permutation p=0.0286, group means scratch rho[dTB]=+0.42 vs pretrained rho[dBT]=+0.61 / rho[dTB]=-0.08), estimator replication, DINO appearance null (p=0.43), and the two-cost mechanism; Sec 5 derives the fit-free regime-aware selection policy (rank by dTB+dBT scratch, dBT pretrained), shows it best on all three hold-out protocols (rho 0.52/0.52/0.50), frames rho~0.5 as the reproducibility ceiling (pretrained fraction 1.08 = parity with retraining a sibling; 73-76% of a 3-architecture consensus at ceiling 0.732), recovers the sign structure with per-regime 2-coefficient OLS, and translates to decisions (median top-1 regret 1.2-2.8 PCK vs 13.9 random); Sec 6 splits absolute prediction into anchors (units) + policy (order), MAE 9.3 / r 0.88 LOTO, pretrained MAE 8.2 / r 0.90; Sec 7 gives interventional support: a pre-registered out-of-sample test on a never-seen generated grid where the off-target cost ranks from-scratch sources on the one benchmark where it varies (FlyingThings rho +0.67, 3.1x spread, vs symmetric -0.28), a closed-loop render-free generator search (+0.93 predicted / +0.87 realized on KITTI-2015, null control -1.6), BFV construct validity (recovered camera-vs-object regimes match target physics), the trial19 case study (scratch rank 1/9 -> pretrained rank 3/9), and a motion x texture 2x2 showing specificity-not-magnitude; Sec 8 Limitations is unusually candid (8/9 flip, pretrained half observational-only and the grid's pretrained arm nominally favors the wrong direction, no interventional test of the scratch missing-support cost, 2 backbone architectures, 3 pre-registered FlowFormer predictions); Sec 9 concludes "select with the policy, design with the direction." All 8 main-text \input tables and all 11 main + 4 supp figures exist on disk. The biggest audit findings: (1) tab_decomp's two object-motion/matte cells (83.2, 42.1) were harvested at 00:02 Jun 11 from a from-scratch run launched 21:08 Jun 10 that was still training (val CSV last written 23:57, exact in-flight maxima 83.2400 / 42.0822) — provisional numbers in a main-text table; (2) Sec 7 prose quotes the grid's pretrained-arm point estimates as +0.64/+0.31/+0.43 but the current intervention_oos.csv TT means are +0.64/+0.21/+0.37 (the CSV is explicitly flagged as live in DRAFT_NOTES); (3) the supplement is one reframe behind the main text — it still says the pretrained grid arm has "only three sources", quotes pre-policy rule rhos (0.50/0.51/0.51), says "1,458 models" where main says 99, uses the banned "fine-tuned" wording, and still makes the "rank training sets better than retraining" claim the main text deliberately retracted to "parity"; (4) two supp references from main (KuBasic/pretrained 2x2 replication; 95% bootstrap CIs for Table 3) point to content that does not exist in supp_main.tex; (5) smaller presentation bugs: RAFT shown with a backbone checkmark inside the from-scratch block of Tables 1-2, the policy bolded as best in tab_utility's both-held pairwise column where matched-direction is higher (0.79 vs 0.78), and a tab_law caption claim ("4 of 9 rows... all from-scratch or near-neutral") whose fourth row is actually pretrained CATs++ frozen.

claims.claim: Study scale: 891 transfer evaluations from 3 architectures in 9 training configurations x 11 synthetic training sets x 9 benchmarks; 99 trained models; peak PCK@0.05; each (benchmark, architecture, variant) triple is a context.
claims.numbers: 891; 3 architectures; 9 training configurations; 11 synthetic training sets; 9 benchmarks; 99 trained models; PCK@0.05

claims.claim: Headline pretrained contrast: symmetric distance vs missing-support-alone correlation on the worst-served architecture (pretrained GLU-Net frozen).
claims.numbers: symmetric rho=+0.33 vs +0.76 for missing support alone

claims.claim: The directional flip holds in 8 of 9 training variants; exact permutation p=0.029 (abstract) / p=0.0286 excluding RAFT from the labeling, p=0.0079 with RAFT in the scratch group (Sec 4); it vanishes in DINO appearance space (flip statistic +0.018, p=0.43).

Group-mean within-context Spearman: scratch rho[dTB]=+0.42 vs rho[dBT]=+0.23; pretrained rho[dBT]=+0.61 vs rho[dTB]=-0.08. Verified arithmetically against tab_law.tex per-variant values (scratch dTB: +0.53,+0.51,+0.31,+0.37,+0.40; pretrained dBT: +0.51,+0.50,+0.67,+0.76).
The two directed distances are anti-correlated within contexts across canonical sources (tight-vs-broad tradeoff), the mechanism for why summing is right from scratch and destructive pretrained.

Scratch regime: symmetric average is the best group-mean predictor (+0.50 vs +0.42 for dTB alone); pretrained: symmetric mean dragged from +0.61 down to +0.39; strongest cells pretrained GLU-Net +0.26/+0.33 (sym) vs +0.67/+0.76 (dBT).
Estimator replication of the flip: epsilon-radius coverage at 4px/16px gives +0.65/+0.91, directional kNN-KL +0.30, all at the permutation floor p=0.0286.

Fit-free regime-aware policy (Eq. 3: D=dTB+dBT scratch, D=dBT pretrained) ranks held-out source / benchmark / both at rho 0.52/0.52/0.50, best of 9 predictor families; summed-distance-everywhere 0.44/0.44/0.46; FID/SW2/MMD 0.34/0.44/0.37; 13-feature motion ridge 0.22/0.36/0.23; appearance ridge -0.11/+0.19/-0.07.

Reproducibility-ceiling framing: same-regime retraining agreement (empirical oracle) is rho ~0.56-0.69; policy fraction 1.08 pretrained (0.612 vs oracle 0.564, claimed as parity) and 0.72 scratch (0.499 vs 0.698, headroom in scratch GLU-Net); vs cross-architecture consensus oracle (ceiling 0.732) policy recovers 73-76%. Verified against ceiling_oracles.csv (pretrained rule_rho mean 0.6124, O2 mean 0.5645) and CONSENSUS_POLICY.csv (fractions 0.762803/0.747084/0.727278, cross_arch_consensus_rho 0.732319).

Per-regime 2-coefficient OLS recovers the sign structure: scratch w[dTB]=-7.57, w[dBT]=-1.08; pretrained w[dTB]=-0.82, w[dBT]=-3.22; pooled -4.57/-2.03. Held-out ranking: scratch fit +0.47/+0.56/+0.48 vs fit-free +0.50; pretrained fit +0.29/+0.50/+0.35 vs fit-free +0.61; pooled +0.40/+0.46/+0.41 vs +0.55. Caption explicitly disclaims coefficient ratios as normalization-sensitive.

Leave-one-architecture-out: scratch weights transfer (rho +0.51--0.65); pretrained fitted weights do NOT transfer between the two backbone architectures (held-out +0.25/+0.46 vs fit-free recall rule's +0.44/+0.67 on the same contexts); no nonlinear combiner (interaction, lexicographic, GBM, etc.) beats the 2-coefficient fit held out.

Decision utility: policy median top-1 regret 1.2/2.1/2.8 PCK (source/bench/both held out) vs matched-direction 3.9/4.7/3.9, summed 3.1/3.1/2.7, DINO 14.7/8.0/14.2, random 13.9; pairwise accuracy (gap>10) policy 0.77/0.78/0.78 vs retraining same-architecture 0.84 and different-architecture 0.78; per-regime split: pretrained matched-direction regret 0.7--2.1 vs sum's ~3.0, scratch sum 3.9--4.1 vs matched direction 5.2--7.9.

claims.claim: Absolute prediction: rho~0.5 caps explainable within-context variance at ~rho^2~0.25; cell-mean anchors + policy: MAE 9.3, r=0.88 (held-out source); per-regime gain calibration: pretrained MAE 8.2, r=0.90; both endpoints unseen: r~0.5 via two-way kernel anchor. (Figure F5 panel stats per DRAFT_NOTES are LOTO r .86/MAE 10.4, LOBO .64/21.8, JOINT .56/29.6.)

Pre-registered out-of-sample test (9 never-seen generated sources, from scratch): FlyingThings is the discriminative cell — off-target mass varies 3.12x and ranks transfer at rho +0.67 while coverage varies 1.26x and gives -0.38; kitti2012 row: 1.04x / +0.92 and 2.63x / +0.30; kitti2015 row: 1.02x / +0.38 and 1.67x / -0.70; KITTI rows declared untestable for motion costs (precision-matched by design, appearance twins). Verified exactly against intervention_oos.csv FF rows (0.6667, -0.3833, spreads 3.1186/1.2623, etc.).
Abstract/intro/Sec-4 quote the grid contrast as 'FlyingThings: directed +0.67, symmetric -0.28'; -0.28 matches the current CSV's FF flyingthings sym = -0.2833.
Closed-loop render-free generator search: KITTI-2015 tuned source margin +0.93 predicted, +0.87 realized; FlyingThings null control predicted ~0, realized -1.6.

BFV construct validity: recovered generator parameters — KITTI-2015 camera dolly Delta 2.18 / object vertical fraction 0.00 (camera-centric); FlyingThings 0.32 / 0.92 (object-centric); full supp table additionally gives # movers 4/2, transl. 0.92/1.41, rot. 0.39/1.36, vert. frac 0.001/0.920.

trial19 case study: rank 1/9 from scratch on KITTI-2015 (+1.2 PCK over the next source), rank 3/9 pretrained inside a <=6 PCK near-ceiling band; grid pretrained transfer band 3--8 PCK vs 15--22 from scratch.
claims.numbers: rank 1/9; +1.2 PCK; rank 3/9; <=6 PCK; 3--8 PCK vs 15--22

claims.claim: Motion x texture 2x2 (GSO assets, from scratch): KITTI-2012 target — camera/HQ 96.5 (bold), camera/matte 91.1, object/HQ 89.5, object/matte 83.2; FlyingThings target — camera/HQ 48.9, camera/matte 43.4, object/HQ 54.4 (bold), object/matte 42.1; off-diagonal near-tie on KITTI (91.1 vs 89.5) grounds the specificity-not-magnitude claim. HQ cells verified vs decomp_cells.csv (96.4753, 91.0916, 89.4922, 48.9347, 43.4237, 54.3852); matte/object cells harvested live from an in-flight run (maxima 83.2400 / 42.0822).

Appearance-stripped twins (bit-identical motion): transfer moves 2.7--9.4 PCK while appearance distance moves ~70% (F7 caption); twins differ <=10 PCK from scratch and ~3 pretrained while motion-type effects span 10--80 PCK (fig:intervsplats caption).

Size/supervision controls: fit-free ranking by dataset size, vector count, or supervision density reaches at most rho=0.27 vs 0.52 for the rule; supp table gives n samples +0.043, n vectors +0.267, baseline rule rho +0.507, shuffle null -0.000, family drops +0.425..+0.544, drop-any-benchmark range [+0.495, +0.532].

Middlebury exclusion: pretrained variants returned 52.6 +/- 4.7 PCK regardless of source (spread 4.7 vs 10--17 elsewhere; scratch spread 15.3); harness defect identified; sensitivity with Middlebury included: flip statistic +0.82 instead of +0.90, rule rho 0.49/0.50/0.52 instead of 0.50/0.51/0.51; largest effect on pretrained oracle fraction (0.554 -> 0.612 rule rho).

Sampling stability: mean-NN distances reach rho >= 0.96 by 5x10^4 vectors and 1.000 at the reference budget; kNN-KL plateaus near rho=0.5 (T->B) and rho=0.2 (B->T) and never stabilizes, motivating support-geometry estimators.

Anchor directionality control: directional anchor interpolation loses to symmetric IDW (held-out-benchmark MAE 16.9 symmetric vs 18.9--24.1 directional; held-out-source 8.6 vs 8.7--10.1) — directionality lives in the ranking term only.
DINO negative-control table: all per-variant correlations weak-to-negative in both directions (range -0.14 to -0.35), no regime structure.

Three pre-registered falsifiable FlowFormer predictions stated in Limitations: from-scratch cells ranked by the summed distance, pretrained cells by missing support alone, and per-regime weights fitted on the three architectures transfer without improving on the fit-free scores.
